source.catalogue: Tai Sin LV Cables catalogue - Appendix B Tables B1.1-B1.8 (current), B2.1-B2.8 (mV/A/m, z value for >=25mm²), Appendix C Tables C1.1-C1.3, C2.1-C2.3.

columns.note: S/N. Numbers itself as soon as anything is entered in the row.
Construction as printed under each product title in the catalogue. Only types available for the Phases in this row are listed. In newer Excel you can type part of the name to search.
Only core counts available for this Cable Type and Phases. Control-cable core counts (7C, 12C, 37C...) are included.
Ambient air temperature. Blank = Ca of 1. Used for every method except D.
Ground temperature for buried cables (method D). Blank = Ca of 1.
Number of circuits / multicore cables grouped together. Blank = Cg of 1.
Soil thermal resistivity in K.m/W, method D only (Table C1.3). Blank = Cs of 1 (2.5 K.m/W reference).
Smallest size for the chosen type, cores and method that meets Ib <= In <= Iz and total VD <= permissible VD. Pick it (or larger) in Cable Size.

TN-S or TT. Blank = the Settings default (TN-S). TN-S: fault current returns through the protective conductors to the source (SS 638:2018 411.4L). TT: it returns through the earth electrode and the ground (411.5).

Earth fault loop impedance at the From board (external to this circuit), in ohms. Blank = Zs at the end of the row whose To matches this From (for TT only when that row is also TT); else, TN-S only, the transformer impedance from Transformer Rating (kVA), then the Settings default. TT: type the value measured or declared at the origin (it includes the electrode and earth return).

columns.header:
Earth Electrode Resistance Ra (Ω)
(TT; blank = Zs)
columns.note: TT only: Ra = resistance of the earth electrode plus the protective conductor connecting it to the exposed-conductive-parts (SS 638:2018 411.5.3L). Blank = Zs is used instead (411.5.3L Note 2). Ignored for TN-S.
Device protecting this circuit. MCB / RCBO type B, C, D give Ia = 5, 10, 20 x In (IEC 60898-1, as in SS 638:2018 Table 41.3L). Fuse / MCCB / ACB: type Ia.

Current that operates the device within the Required Disconnection Time. MCCB / ACB: 1.2 x the instantaneous setting (IEC 60947-2 8.2.1.2.4, ±20 % tolerance). Fuse: from its curve at the required time. Blank = 5 / 10 / 20 x In for MCB / RCBO type B / C / D.

columns.header:
RCD Rated Residual Current IΔn (mA)
(blank = no RCD)
columns.note: Rated residual operating current of the RCD, RCCB or RCBO protecting this circuit, in mA (30, 100, 300, 500). Gives the RCD limit 50 V / IΔn: TN-S Zs x IΔn ≤ 50 V (SS 638:2018 411.4.5L), TT Ra x IΔn ≤ 50 V (411.5.3L, Table 41.5). Blank = no RCD.

SS 638:2018 Table 41.1 by earthing system and nominal U0 for a final circuit (In ≤ 32 A and its To feeds no other row), 411.3.2.2L: TN-S 0.4 s, TT 0.2 s for 120 V < U0 ≤ 230 V. Otherwise TN-S 5 s (411.3.2.3L), TT 1 s (411.3.2.4L).

What carries the earth fault back. Blank = Earth core in cable for 5C 3-phase, 3C 1-phase and 3C+3E cables, else Separate copper conductor. Pick Steel armour, Aluminium armour or Copper tape screen when the cable metalwork is the CPC.

Protective conductor cross-section per cable. Blank: full-size earth core = Cable Size; reduced earth core or separate conductor = IEC 60364-5-54 Table 54.2 minimum. Armour and copper tape: type the area from the cable catalogue.
Protective conductor resistance per metre at 20°C. Blank = IEC 60228 copper value for the CPC size. Armour and copper tape: type the value from the cable catalogue.

IEC 60364-5-54 543.1.1 and Table 54.2: S ≤ 16: S; 16 < S ≤ 35: 16; S > 35: S/2, rounded up to a standard size for copper. Steel or aluminium armour: x k1/k2. Separate conductor at least 2.5 mm² (543.1.3, mechanically protected).
(Phase resistance x its multiplier + CPC resistance x its multiplier) x Cable Run / (1000 x no. of cables). Multipliers take each conductor to its operating temperature (FaultData).
Zs = Ze + R1+R2. Shows Enter Ze when no Ze is typed, fed from another row, given by a transformer (TN-S) or set in Settings (TN-S).

The larger of the overcurrent and RCD limits. TN-S (SS 638:2018 411.4.5L): Zs x Ia ≤ U0 or Zs x IΔn ≤ 50 V, so Cmin x U0 / Ia or 50 / IΔn (Cmin from Settings, 1; U0 nominal, 230 V on a 400 V system). TT: Ra x IΔn ≤ 50 V (411.5.3L) or Ra x Ia ≤ 50 V (411.5.4L), so 50 / IΔn or 50 / Ia.
Prospective earth fault current at the far end: If = U0 / Zs.

columns.header:
Earth Loop Check
(Zs or Ra ≤ Max)
columns.note: PASS when the device disconnects an earth fault within the Required Disconnection Time: TN-S Zs ≤ Max Zs; TT Ra (or Zs when Ra is blank) ≤ Max.
Table 54.2 when the CPC is at least the table minimum (selected, 543.1.1, no calculation needed). Adiabatic when it is smaller (calculated, 543.1.2). Enter CPC size: type the armour or tape area.

Table 54.2: PASS by selection. Adiabatic (IEC 60364-5-54 543.1.2): PASS when (k x S x no. of cables)² ≥ If² x t, t = Fault Clearance Time if typed, else the Required Disconnection Time; the let-through energy is used when smaller.

Prospective fault current at the From board in kA (3-phase symmetrical for 3-phase circuits). Blank = Fault Level at To of the row whose To matches this From; else the transformer fault level from Transformer Rating (kVA); else the Settings default.
Rated breaking capacity of the protective device: Icu for an MCCB / ACB (IEC 60947-2), Icn for an MCB (IEC 60898-1), from the device data.

columns.header:
Breaking Capacity Check
(≥ Fault Level at From)
columns.note: IEC 60364-4-43:2023 431.5.4.1: the device must break the maximum prospective fault current where it is installed (or be backed up by a supply-side device, 431.6.3.2).
Time the protective device takes to clear the fault. Blank = Settings default (0.1 s) for the short-circuit check and the Required Disconnection Time for the CPC check.
Device let-through energy at this fault level, from the manufacturer's data. Needed for clearance below 0.1 s (IEC 60364-4-43:2023 431.5.4.2), e.g. current-limiting MCBs. Blank = Ik² x t.
Fault level at the To end: the From level reduced by the cable resistance at 20°C (phase conductor for 3-phase, phase + neutral for 1-phase). Feeds the rows supplied from this To.

columns.header: Min Cable Size for Short Circuit (mm²)
columns.note: √(I²t) / (k x no. of cables), k from IEC 60364-4-43:2023 Table 2 (115 PVC, 103 PVC above 300 mm², 143 XLPE).
PASS when Cable Size ≥ Min Cable Size (IEC 60364-4-43:2023 431.5.4.2). An MCB clears in under 0.1 s, so Ik² x t overstates its energy: Check let-through means type its let-through I²t.
How the motor starts: DOL, Star-delta, Soft starter or VFD. Leave blank for loads that are not motors; the starting voltage drop columns then stay blank.

Starting current as a multiple of the design current Ib. Blank = the starter type's typical value on Lists (DOL 6, Star-delta 2, Soft starter 3, VFD 1). Type the motor's locked-rotor ratio (Ia/In) when you have it.

Voltage drop at the motor while it starts: total VD at the From board (running) + this cable's VD at the starting current (Circuit VD % x Starting Current). Uses the tabulated mV/A/m, which covers the low power factor at starting. The extra starting current in the upstream feeders is not added. Blank until From, Starter Type and the circuit VD are filled.
Largest voltage drop allowed at the motor while it starts, in %. Blank = Settings (15 %). Use the figure in your project specification.
PASS when Starting VD (%) is not more than Permissible Starting VD (%).

G.error: Enter a load in kW (0 or more).

I.error: Power factor must be between 0.01 and 1.

L.error: Enter THD as a decimal, e.g. 0.2 for 20%.

U.error: Enter a whole number of grouped circuits.

W.error: Enter soil thermal resistivity in K.m/W, e.g. 1.5.

Y.error: Rating factor must be between 0.01 and 1.5.

Z.error: Rating factor must be between 0.01 and 1.5.

AQ.error: Enter the earth fault loop impedance at the From board in ohms (0 or more).

AR.error: Enter the earth electrode resistance Ra in ohms (0 or more).

AT.error: Enter the disconnection current Ia in amps.

AU.error: Enter the RCD rated residual operating current IΔn in mA (for example 30, 100, 300).

AX.error: Enter the protective conductor cross-section in mm² (above 0).

AY.error: Enter the protective conductor resistance at 20°C in mΩ/m (above 0).

BH.error: Enter the prospective fault current at the From board in kA.

BI.error: Enter the device breaking capacity in kA.

BK.error: Enter a value above 0 (seconds for the clearance time, A²s for the let-through energy).

BL.error: Enter a value above 0 (seconds for the clearance time, A²s for the let-through energy).

BQ.error: Enter the starting current as a multiple of Ib (1 or more), e.g. 6.

BS.error: Enter permissible starting VD in %, e.g. 15.

listError: Pick a value from the list. If the list is empty, fill in the cells to the left first.

fault.sources: Sources: conductor resistance = IEC 60228 Table 2 (class 2 plain copper, max. d.c. resistance at 20°C); k line conductor = IEC 60364-4-43:2023 Table 2; k CPC = IEC 60364-5-54:2011 Tables A.54.4 (core in a cable), A.54.2 (separate conductor, PVC-insulated, not bunched) and A.54.5 (armour, tape); resistance multiplier = (β + θi) / (β + 20), β and initial temperatures from IEC 60364-5-54 Annex A (copper 234.5, aluminium 228, steel 202); Ia multiples = top of the IEC 60898-1 instantaneous trip bands (SS 638:2018 Table 41.3L); disconnection times = SS 638:2018 Table 41.1 (TN-S and TT, a.c., final circuits up to 32 A; other circuits 5 s TN-S, 411.3.2.3L, and 1 s TT, 411.3.2.4L); Uz = IEC 60076-5 Table 1 (minimum short-circuit impedance of distribution transformers).

factorSources: Sources: temperature = Tables C1.1 (AIR) / C1.2 (GROUND); grouping = Table C2.1 (BUNCHED / WALL / TRAY), Table C2.2 cables touching (GROUND_DIRECT), Table C2.3(i) ducts touching (GROUND_DUCT), >6 circuits in ground uses 6; soil = Table C1.3.
notes: 1. Voltage Drop Check stays blank until you enter the Permissible VD (%) for that row.

2. Fill in left to right: From/To -> Phases -> Voltage -> Load, PF -> Protection (typed) -> Cable Type -> No. of Cores -> Installation Method -> (temperatures, grouping, soil) -> Cable Size -> No. of cables -> Cable Run.
3. Item (S/N) numbers itself 1, 2, 3... as soon as anything is typed in a row; empty rows are skipped. If you insert a row, copy the Item formula into it.
4. Each dropdown only lists options valid for the cells to its left (3-phase hides 2-core; cores depend on cable type; methods depend on type + cores; sizes depend on type + cores + method).
5. If you change an earlier cell after filling later ones, the now-invalid cells turn red - pick again.

6. Cable Type = the construction in standard shorthand (the PVC bedding layer directly under the armour or screen is dropped, e.g. catalogue Cu/XLPE/PVC/SWA/PVC = Cu/XLPE/SWA/PVC), so cables from other catalogues with the same construction fit the same type. The voltage grade is added in brackets only where one construction exists in two grades: Cu/PVC (450/750V) and Cu/PVC (0.6/1kV). The catalogue construction names and Tai Sin product codes are listed on the CableTypes and Cores sheets.

7. Scope: PVC-sheathed Cu/PVC and Cu/XLPE cables (incl. AWA armoured single cores and CT copper-tape screened), plus Cu/XLPE/SWA/LSOH (catalogue FRT-XSH, Cu/XLPE/LSZH/SWA/LSZH - LSOH and LSZH mean the same). Other LSZH and fire-resistant mica-taped (FR range) cables are not included.

8. Power and control versions of the same construction and core count are merged (e.g. Cu/PVC/PVC 4C = PPM 4C + PCC 4C). On 1-phase, 3/4/5-core cables only offer the control-cable sizes (1.5 - 4 mm²).

9. Rating factors: every blank input gives a factor of 1. Ca uses Ambient Air Temp for all methods except D, and Ground Temp for method D (Tables C1.1 / C1.2); temperatures are rounded UP to the next 5°C row. Above the table limit (PVC 60°C air, XLPE 80°C) shows "Out of range".

10. Cg (No. of Grouped Circuits): methods A/B = "bunched" row, C = "single layer on wall", E/F/G = "single layer on perforated tray" (Table C2.1); D direct in ground = Table C2.2 cables touching; D in ducts = Table C2.3(i) ducts touching (more than 6 uses 6). Counts between table columns use the next higher count.

11. Cs (Soil Thermal Resistivity, K.m/W): only applies to method D (Table C1.3, "buried ducts" or "direct buried" row). Values between table points use the next higher resistivity; above 3 K.m/W shows "Out of range". For all other methods Cs = 1.
12. Ci and Ct have no table in the catalogue: type the factor (blank = 1).
13. Data source: Tai Sin LV Cables catalogue - Appendix B Tables B1.1-B1.8 (current), B2.1-B2.8 (mV/A/m, z value for >=25mm²), Appendix C Tables C1.1-C1.3, C2.1-C2.3.
14. Single-core 3-phase clipped direct (method C) uses the flat-touching mV/A/m (slightly higher than trefoil).
15. Non-sheathed single cores - Cu/PVC (450/750V) and Cu/PVC (0.6/1kV) - are limited to methods A and B (must be enclosed).
16. Control cables use the rating table the catalogue refers to (2-core column for 1-phase, 3/4-core column for 3-phase). No reduction is applied for many loaded cores.

17. Suggested Cable Size = smallest size for the chosen type + cores + method that meets Ib <= In <= Iz AND total VD <= permissible VD (the VD condition is only applied once Permissible VD is entered for that row).
18. Total VD: the row whose "To" matches this row's "From" is treated as the upstream feeder and its total VD is added.
19. Protection Rating In is typed in manually (amps). It turns red if it is below the design current Ib.
20. To add a voltage or transformer size, add it to the list on the Lists sheet.

1. Earthing System (AP): TN-S or TT per row; blank = the Settings default. TN-S: the fault returns through the protective conductors (SS 638:2018 411.4L). TT: it returns through the earth electrode and the ground (411.5).

2. Earth fault loop: Zs = Ze + R1+R2. TN-S (411.4.5L): PASS when Zs x Ia ≤ U0 or Zs x IΔn ≤ 50 V, so Max Zs = the larger of Cmin x U0 / Ia and 50 / IΔn. TT: PASS when Ra x IΔn ≤ 50 V (411.5.3L, RCD, preferred by 411.5.2) or Ra x Ia ≤ 50 V (411.5.4L, overcurrent device), Ra = earth electrode + its protective conductor, or Zs when Ra is not known (411.5.3L Note 2). U0 is the nominal line-to-earth voltage: the voltage for 1-phase, voltage / √3 rounded to 10 V for 3-phase (400 V gives 230 V).

3. Ia: MCB / RCBO type B, C, D = 5, 10, 20 x In (IEC 60898-1; the same values give SS 638 Table 41.3L). MCCB / ACB: type 1.2 x the instantaneous setting (IEC 60947-2 8.2.1.2.4, ±20 % tolerance) or the curve current at the required time. Fuses: the curve current at the required time (SS 638 Tables 41.2 and 41.4). IΔn: the RCD rated residual operating current in mA (Table 41.5: 30 mA gives 1667 Ω).

4. Required Disconnection Time (SS 638 Table 41.1, a.c.): final circuits up to 32 A (In ≤ 32 A and the To feeds no other row), for U0 up to 120 / 230 / 400 V / above: TN-S 0.8 / 0.4 / 0.2 / 0.1 s, TT 0.3 / 0.2 / 0.07 / 0.04 s (411.3.2.2L). Other circuits: TN-S 5 s (411.3.2.3L), TT 1 s (411.3.2.4L). If it cannot be met, see 411.3.2.6L (supplementary bonding).

5. R1+R2 = (r1 x m1 + r2 x m2) x Cable Run / (1000 x no. of cables). r at 20°C: IEC 60228 for copper conductors, the catalogue value for armour or tape. m = (β + θi) / (β + 20) with β and the initial temperature θi of each conductor from IEC 60364-5-54 Annex A (FaultData).

6. CPC (IEC 60364-5-54 543.1.1): CPC Type blank = Earth core in cable for 5C 3-phase, 3C 1-phase (full size) and 3C+3E cables, else Separate copper conductor. Table 54.2 minimum: S ≤ 16: S; 16 < S ≤ 35: 16; S > 35: S/2 (copper, rounded up to a standard size; separate conductor at least 2.5 mm², 543.1.3); steel or aluminium armour x k1/k2. A CPC at least that size passes by selection. A smaller one is calculated (543.1.2): (k2 x S x no. of cables)² ≥ If² x t, t = Fault Clearance Time or else the Required Disconnection Time, or the let-through energy if smaller.

7. k values: line conductors IEC 60364-4-43:2023 Table 2; CPC IEC 60364-5-54 Tables A.54.4 (core in a cable), A.54.2 (separate conductor, taken as PVC-insulated and not bunched) and A.54.5 (armour, tape).

8. Ze at From: a typed value wins; else the row whose To matches this row's From supplies its Zs (for a TT row only when that row is also TT); else, TN-S only, the Transformer Rating (kVA) gives the transformer's own impedance (Uz from FaultData, infinite upstream source), then the Settings default. TT rows need Ze typed (measured or declared, including the electrode and earth return) or a TT feeding row. Fault Level at From chains the same way for both systems (row above, transformer, Settings). Blank From means no feeding row.

9. Short circuit (IEC 60364-4-43:2023 431.5.4): Breaking Capacity ≥ Fault Level at From (431.5.4.1). Cable: k²S² ≥ I²t at the Fault Level at From (431.5.4.2); I²t = let-through energy if typed, else Ik² x t. Below 0.1 s the manufacturer's let-through must be used, so an MCB row that fails on Ik² x t shows Check let-through. Fault Level at To = From level reduced by the cable resistance at 20°C.

10. Not modelled: TN-C, TN-C-S and IT systems, cable reactance (Zs reads low above about 35 mm²), the voltage factor c and minimum fault currents (IEC 60909), RCD discrimination (531.2.9L), TN-S times for a bonded TT installation on an overcurrent device (Table 41.1 note), electrode stability above 200 Ω (542.2.4).
